cards.explanation: The answer is rejected. Samuel doesn't dance around it, friends. He says, “But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions…” (1 Samuel 10:19). Then he quotes what they told God: “No, set a king over us.” That's a heavy moment, and I think this one hurts.

The answer is Benjamin! Samuel has all the tribes of Israel come forward, and “…the tribe of Benjamin was selected.” (1 Samuel 10:20). Think of a giant bakery order getting sorted into one tray. Everything starts big and it's about to get a LOT smaller.

The answer is Saul son of Kish. After the tribe and the clan, “Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected.” (1 Samuel 10:21). It goes from the tribe of Benjamin, to the clan of Matri, to one man. One name, friends, and it's his.

The answer is that they inquire of the LORD again, asking, “Has the man come here yet?” (1 Samuel 10:22). They ask the LORD, and He tells them where Saul is. That's a good habit for any of us when something goes missing.

The answer is hidden! The LORD replies, “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.” (1 Samuel 10:22). Think about that for a second, bakers. They looked for him and could not find him, and there he is, tucked in among the baggage. The text doesn't tell us why he hid, and I won't guess.

The answer is king. The people shout, “Long live the king!” (1 Samuel 10:24). Samuel has just asked, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” And the crowd answers with a roar. After all that searching, I bet that shout felt GOOD.

The answer is before the LORD. Samuel “…wrote them on a scroll and laid it up before the LORD.” (1 Samuel 10:25). He doesn't just say the rights of kingship out loud and walk off, friends. He writes them down and sets them in front of the LORD. That's a scroll with a very good home.

The answer is False, and it's good news for Saul. He goes home to Gibeah, and “…the men of valor whose hearts God had touched went with him.” (1 Samuel 10:26). Samuel sends everybody home, but Saul doesn't walk back by himself. Those men go along with him.

The answer is “How can this man save us?” Some worthless men said it (1 Samuel 10:27). It's a pointed question. They despised him and brought him no gifts. The text doesn't give us their reasons, so I'll leave that open too.

The answer is that he stays silent about it. The text says, “but Saul remained silent about it.” (1 Samuel 10:27). Those men despised him and brought no gifts, and he doesn't answer back. I can't say what Saul was feeling, but I think that took some restraint. If somebody sniffed at me in a meeting, I'd have a speech ready before the timer dinged.
